name: Connor
title: 12-Week Beginner Strength Plan - Connor (age 9)
intro: Upper/Lower split, 3 sessions/week, ~30 minutes. Mostly bodyweight, TRX straps, and form practice with a broomstick or very light Bowflex dumbbells (5 lb to start). All targets are conservative starting points - adjust to what Connor can do with slow, controlled, good-form reps.

warmup.label: 1. Get warm (2 min)
warmup.text: Jumping jacks, jog in place, skipping, or jump rope. Make it a game: 'Simon says' or follow-the-leader.

warmup.label: 2. Mobility (2 min)
warmup.text: 10 arm circles each way, 10 bodyweight squats, 5 inchworms, 5 bird dogs per side, 10 calf raises.

warmup.label: 3. Practice (1 min)
warmup.text: 5 slow practice reps of the first exercise with no weight (or a broomstick), focusing on form.

cooldown.label: Cool-down (3 min)
cooldown.text: Easy walk, then gentle stretches held 15-20 sec: quads, hamstrings, calves, chest in a doorway, child's pose. Give the sticker / checkmark!

items.label: Primary goal
items.text: Have fun, learn safe movement (squat, lunge, hinge, push, pull, core) and build a habit of moving and training with Dad.

items.label: Secondary goal
items.text: Slow, steady strength gains through more reps, slower reps and harder versions - NOT heavy weight. Good form always beats more reps or more weight.

items.label: Starting numbers
items.text: Unknown - so the plan starts conservatively. Week 1 is a BASELINE week: the numbers Connor writes down (reps, hold times, squats in 60 sec, max good-form push-ups, longest plank and hang) become his baseline. Targets will be adjusted after Justin sends back each week's results.

items.label: Phases
items.text:
Weeks 1-4: LEARN (learn the movements, 1-2 sets; easy week in week 4)
Weeks 5-8: BUILD (2-3 sets, harder versions; easy week in week 8)
Weeks 9-12: CHALLENGE (2-3 sets, harder versions / tiny weight only if EASY; week 12 is a FUN REP-RECORD week compared to week 1 - bodyweight only, NO max lifts).

items.label: Days
items.text: 3 sessions per week (e.g., Mon / Wed / Fri, or fit around sports practices), about 30 minutes each.

items.label: THE RULE
items.text: Upper and Lower days can be done on back-to-back days (e.g., around practices), but NEVER do two of the same type (Upper + Upper or Lower + Lower) on consecutive days. Aim for at least one full rest day each week, and skip or go light on Lower day right before a game if legs are tired.

items.label: Lower / Upper rotation
items.text: Alternate Lower and Upper days. Odd weeks (1,3,5,7,9,11): Lower, Upper, Lower. Even weeks (2,4,6,8,10,12): Upper, Lower, Upper. The days keep alternating across weeks (L-U-L | U-L-U | L-U-L ...), and each day type is done 18 times over the 12 weeks.

items.label: LOWER day
items.text: Squat (box squat to bench, TRX for balance at first) | Reverse lunge (TRX-assisted at first) | Glute bridge | Broomstick hip hinge / RDL (form practice) | Step-up (low step) | Calf raises | Plank (+ side planks from week 5) | Fun challenge.

items.label: UPPER day
items.text: Push-ups (incline on rack bar -> bench -> floor) | One-arm row (Bowflex 5 lb) | Lat pulldown (light) | TRX row (body angle sets the difficulty) | Overhead press (broomstick -> Bowflex 5 lb) | Dead hang (flexed-arm hang option from week 9) | Dead bug | Fun challenge.

items.label: Session length (~30 min)
items.text: 5-min warm-up + ~20 min of exercises + 2-min fun challenge + 3-min cool-down. Rest 45-60 sec between sets. To save time, pair two exercises and go back and forth (e.g., squat then plank, push-ups then row).

items.label: 1. Get warm (2 min)
items.text: Jumping jacks, jog in place, skipping, or jump rope. Make it a game: 'Simon says' or follow-the-leader.

items.label: 2. Mobility (2 min)
items.text: 10 arm circles each way, 10 bodyweight squats, 5 inchworms, 5 bird dogs per side, 10 calf raises.

items.label: 3. Practice (1 min)
items.text: 5 slow practice reps of the first exercise with no weight (or a broomstick), focusing on form.

items.label: Cool-down (3 min)
items.text: Easy walk, then gentle stretches held 15-20 sec: quads, hamstrings, calves, chest in a doorway, child's pose. Give the sticker / checkmark!

items.label: Stickers & checkmarks
items.text: Each finished session = a sticker or checkmark on the weekly log. Each fun challenge = a bonus sticker. Finishing the 12 weeks = a celebration (Connor picks the reward).

items.label: Games & challenges
items.text: Every session ends with a short fun challenge (bear crawls, wall sits, balance, wheelbarrow walk...). Let Connor pick the music, count reps out loud, or 'coach' Dad for a set.

items.label: Record board
items.text: Write week-1 baseline numbers on the Progress Log and compare them in week 12. Celebrate effort and good form, not just numbers.

items.label: How it works
items.text: Most exercises use 12-15 reps (or a time/per-side target). Keep the same version until ALL sets feel EASY with good form, then make ONE small change next session: add 1-2 reps, add a set, slow the lowering (3 sec), or move to the next harder version.

items.label: Weight increases
items.text: Only on the Bowflex dumbbell exercises, and only after all sets feel EASY with good form: one 2.5 lb step at a time (5 -> 7.5 lb, and 10 lb only in weeks 9-11). Lat pulldown: the smallest plate is 5 lb, so progress with reps and slow returns first; +5 lb only late in the plan if 3 x 15 is EASY. TRX rows get harder by moving the feet one small step closer to the anchor, not by adding weight. Never add weight and reps at the same time. If form slips, go back to the last version.

items.label: Sets
items.text: 1-2 sets in weeks 1-4, building to 2-3 sets in weeks 5-11. Main exercises reach 3 sets; small exercises stay at 1-2.

items.label: Targets
items.text: Targets in the plan are SUGGESTIONS ONLY. If a target feels HARD, stay at the previous version. If it feels too easy, still only make one small change.

items.label: Easy (deload) weeks 4 and 8
items.text: Fewer sets (usually 1-2) and easier versions so the body can recover and form stays sharp. Still fun challenges!

items.label: Week 12 - fun rep-record week
items.text: Light week plus record tests compared to week 1: max good-form push-ups (same height as week 1), longest good-form plank, squats in 60 sec (same bench), longest dead hang. Bodyweight only. NO one-rep max tests, no heavy maxes, never to failure - stop the first time a rep isn't clean.

items.label: Adult supervision
items.text: An adult supervises EVERY session. No training alone, and no using the bars, rack or plates without an adult.

items.label: Form over weight
items.text: Good form always wins. If form breaks down, end the set. Leave 2-3 reps 'in the tank' - nothing to failure.

items.label: Stop if pain
items.text: Stop immediately for sharp pain or any joint pain (knees, back, shoulders, elbows, wrists, heels). Normal muscle burn/tiredness is OK; pain is not. If pain continues, check with a doctor.

items.label: No max testing
items.text: No one-rep max (1RM) tests, ever. Progress is measured with good-form reps and hold times.

items.label: Slow, controlled reps
items.text: About 2-3 seconds down, controlled up. No bouncing, jerking or swinging.

items.label: Hydrate & recover
items.text: Water before, during and after. Sleep 9-12 hours per night. Regular meals with protein, fruits and vegetables. Rest days matter, especially on heavy practice weeks.

items.label: Rack safeties set
items.text: Keep the power rack safeties set (and pins locked) whenever the rack is used, including for incline push-ups on the bar. Keep heavy plates, bars and the 25/45 lb dumbbells stored and out of the way.

items.label: Bowflex dumbbells
items.text: An adult sets the weight (or teaches Connor to do it and checks every time): dumbbell sitting in its tray, turn BOTH end dials to the same number, then lift it straight up. Put it back level in the tray. Never drop it or set it down anywhere but the tray.

items.label: TRX straps
items.text: An adult checks the anchor and strap length before each use. Straps stay tight (no slack) during every rep. Feet on a non-slip floor.

items.label: Environment
items.text: Clear floor space, flat stable shoes, no loose plates on the floor, adult close by at the pull-up bar and dip handles.

items.label: Bowflex SelectTech 52 dumbbells
items.text: Adjustable 5-52.5 lb per hand in 2.5 lb steps - this is Connor's main 'weight' now. Start at 5 lb for rows, overhead press, goblet squats and RDLs; 7.5 lb and then 10 lb only in later weeks and only after ALL sets feel EASY. Each end has its own dial: with the dumbbell sitting in its tray, turn BOTH dials to the same number. An adult sets them (or teaches Connor to and checks every time).

items.label: TRX straps
items.text: TRX rows on Upper days (body angle controls difficulty: more upright = easier). On Lower days in weeks 1-4, hold the handles lightly for balance on box squats and reverse lunges. Adult checks the anchor and strap length.

items.label: Mikolo F4 power rack + safeties
items.text: Bar or safeties set at hip height = incline push-up station (lower it hole by hole as Connor gets stronger). Hold the upright for balance on step-ups and calf raises. Safeties always set.

items.label: Pull-up bar
items.text: Dead hangs (adult lifts him up or he steps up from a sturdy box). From week 9, flexed-arm hang: step up so the chin is over the bar and hold. No band needed. Let go before the grip gives out.

items.label: Lat pulldown / low row attachment
items.text: Lat pulldown with NOTHING loaded - the handle/carriage still has some resistance. Write it down: ___ lb. Progress with reps and slow returns; +5 lb only late in the plan if 3 x 15 is EASY. The low row is not used (TRX rows replace it); it can be a swap for TRX rows on a day the straps aren't set up, nothing loaded.

items.label: Landmine
items.text: Not used in this plan - it needs the Olympic bar, which is too heavy for now.

items.label: Dip handles
items.text: Support holds only (3 x 5-10 sec, arms straight, shoulders down) as an occasional fun challenge from week 5. No dips yet. Skip if shoulders feel uncomfortable.

items.label: Flat bench
items.text: Box-squat target, one-arm row support, and incline push-up station (weeks 9+). There is no leg extension attachment anymore - step-ups on a low step replace leg extensions.

items.label: Low step for step-ups
items.text: A sturdy, non-slip step about 6-8 inches high (e.g., the bottom stair or an aerobic step). The flat bench is too high for step-ups for now.

items.label: Barbells: CAP Boss Olympic bar (on order), old 30 lb bar
items.text: Too heavy for now - DON'T USE. Use a broomstick for bar practice.

items.label: 15 lb EZ curl bar
items.text: Not scheduled in the plan. Optional only in weeks 10-11: 1 set of 10-12 EZ-bar curls in place of the last row set, ONLY if 7.5 lb Bowflex rows and presses are EASY with perfect form and an adult hands him the bar. If in doubt, save it for the next plan.

items.label: Plate-loaded dumbbell handles (2-inch, 9 lb each)
items.text: Not used - 9 lb empty is too big a starting load for Connor, and the Bowflex covers small steps.

items.label: Olympic plates
items.text: 2 x 45, 2 x 25, 8 x 10, 4 x 5 lb (no 2.5s). The 45 lb plate laid flat is the step for calf raises. Plates are only used for the calf-raise step and (late, optional) +5 lb on the pulldown.

items.label: Fixed dumbbells 25 and 45 lb
items.text: Too heavy - don't use.

items.label: Optional: pair of 2.5 lb plates
items.text: No longer needed for dumbbell work (the Bowflex covers 2.5 lb steps). Optional only for smaller steps on the lat pulldown.

items.label: Low sturdy step (6-8 in)
items.text: Only if there is no safe bottom stair to use for step-ups.

items.label: Stickers + a small calendar
items.text: For tracking sessions and fun challenges.

guide.name: Bird dog (warm-up)
guide.how: On hands and knees, back flat like a table. Reach one arm forward and the opposite leg back, hold 2 sec without tipping, return and switch.

guide.name: Inchworm (warm-up)
guide.how: Stand, fold forward and put hands on the floor, walk the hands out to a push-up position, then walk the feet up to the hands and stand.

guide.name: Box squat -> bodyweight squat -> goblet squat
guide.how: Feet shoulder width, chest up. Sit back and down until you lightly touch the bench, then stand up tall - no plopping. Later: same squat without the bench, then with a pause, then holding one 5 lb Bowflex dumbbell at the chest (goblet) only if all sets feel EASY. TRX-assisted (weeks 1-4): hold both TRX handles lightly in front, straps tight, just for balance - the legs do the work.

guide.name: Reverse lunge / split squat
guide.how: Stand tall, step one foot back and lower the back knee gently toward the floor. Front knee stays over the middle of the foot. Push through the front heel to come back up. Weeks 1-4: hold both TRX handles in front for balance (light grip, legs do the work). Split squat = feet stay in place, just go down and up.

guide.name: Glute bridge (and single-leg bridge)
guide.how: Lie on your back, knees bent, feet flat. Squeeze your glutes and push through your heels to lift your hips until knees, hips and shoulders line up, pause, lower slowly. Single-leg: one foot up, same thing.

guide.name: Broomstick hip hinge / RDL
guide.how: Hinge: broomstick along the back touching the head, upper back and tailbone. Soft knees, push hips BACK until you feel the back of the legs stretch, keep all 3 touch points, stand up by squeezing glutes. RDL: hold the stick (later two 5 lb Bowflex dumbbells) at the thighs, slide it down to just below the knees with a flat back, stand up.

guide.name: Step-up (low step)
guide.how: Stand facing a sturdy low step (6-8 in). Put the WHOLE foot on the step, push through that heel to stand up tall on top, then step down slowly with the same leg - no jumping or pushing off the back foot. Do all reps on one leg, then switch. Hold the rack for balance at first.

guide.name: Calf raises
guide.how: Hold the rack for balance. Rise up onto your toes, pause, lower slowly. Later: balls of feet on the edge of a 45 lb plate laid flat, then one leg at a time.

guide.name: Plank and side plank
guide.how: Plank: forearms on the floor, body in a straight line head to heels, squeeze glutes and belly, breathe. Side plank: on one forearm and the side of the feet (or knees to make it easier), hips up in a straight line. Stop when hips sag.

guide.name: Push-ups (incline -> floor)
guide.how: Hands on the rack bar/safeties (set at hip height, pins locked) a bit wider than shoulders, body straight like a plank. Lower your chest to the bar and push back up. Lower the bar one hole at a time, then hands on the bench, then the floor. Higher hands = easier.

guide.name: One-arm row (dumbbell handle)
guide.how: One hand and the same-side knee on the bench, flat back. Hold a Bowflex dumbbell (5 lb to start, set by an adult) in the other hand, pull it up to the hip, squeeze the shoulder blade, lower slowly. Do all reps, then switch.

guide.name: Lat pulldown (light)
guide.how: Grip the bar a little wider than shoulders. Pull it down to the upper chest by driving the elbows down, without leaning back or yanking, then let it rise slowly. Start with nothing loaded.

guide.name: TRX row
guide.how: Hold both handles, arms straight, and walk the feet forward until the body leans back in a straight line (like a standing plank). Pull the chest up to the hands, squeeze the shoulder blades, lower slowly. Body almost upright = easy; feet a step closer to the anchor = harder. Change only one small step at a time. Adult checks the anchor and that straps stay tight.

guide.name: Overhead press (broomstick -> Bowflex 5 lb)
guide.how: Stand tall, squeeze glutes, ribs down. Hold the broomstick (later two 5 lb Bowflex dumbbells) at the shoulders, press straight up until arms are by the ears, lower slowly to the shoulders.

guide.name: Dead hang / flexed-arm hang
guide.how: Dead hang: adult lifts him to the bar (or step up), hands shoulder width, arms long, shoulders pulled slightly away from ears, hold. Flexed-arm hang (week 9+): step up so the chin is over the bar, hold. Let go before the grip gives out and step down - don't drop.

guide.name: Dead bug
guide.how: Lie on your back with arms reaching up and knees bent at 90 degrees. Keep the low back pressed into the floor and slowly reach the opposite arm and leg out, breathe out, return and switch sides.

guide.name: Dip-handle support hold (fun challenge)
guide.how: Adult close by. Hands on the dip handles, jump or step up to straight arms, shoulders pushed DOWN away from the ears, hold 5-10 sec. No dipping. Skip if shoulders feel uncomfortable.

guide.name: Bowflex dumbbell - setting the weight
guide.how: Adult job (or Connor once taught, with an adult checking): dumbbell sitting in its tray, turn BOTH end dials to the same number, lift it straight up out of the tray. To change weight, put it back level in the tray first. Never drop it.

guide.name: Fun challenges
guide.how: Short games at the end of each session (bear crawl, crab walk, wall sit, balance, wheelbarrow walk, plank high-fives...). Good form beats speed. Each one earns a sticker or checkmark.
